consistency_feedback:
Key inconsistencies and gaps
1. Missing real results.  Nearly every table and figure is labelled “Expected” or is a placeholder to be “filled after runs”.  No numeric FID, FLOPs or p-values that substantiate the headline “2–3× speed-up at equal FID” are reported.  The only concrete log shows a short 3-epoch CNN training that is unrelated to DHAC.
2. No statistical support.  Although the protocol promises mean ± std over three seeds and t-tests, no actual variances, confidence intervals or test statistics are given.  Conclusions about “ρ>0.7”, “precision≈0.8”, “ΔFID<0.5” therefore have no evidential backing.
3. Internal contradiction.  The global settings say batch-size = 128 for 64×64 images on a 16 GB T4 with activation checkpointing, but Experiment 1 later profiles with torch.profiler (which keeps every activation) over 256 images.  Memory would exceed 16 GB, contradicting the earlier claim that everything fits.
4. Reproducibility gaps.  • Random seeds are listed, yet no seed-specific results are output.  • The flops_per_image helper counts FLOPs on a single dummy input, but speed-up claims are made for block-sparse execution that the dummy pass does not activate, inflating the “FLOPs saved”.
5. Controls not executed.  Baselines (original UNet, ASE) are never actually sampled; therefore the Pareto dominance statement is unverified.
6. Energy measurement unclear.  Instantaneous power is integrated for the whole job, but comparisons normalise per-image only for DHAC, not for baselines – apples-to-oranges.

Actionable roadmap to reach consistency_score 8-10
A. Run the experiments and publish the raw numbers.
   • For every λ produce a table: FID (mean ± std over 3 seeds), FLOPs/img, ms/img, J/img.
   • Release csv + json as promised so reviewers can recompute statistics.
B. Strengthen statistical analysis.
   • Use 50 k samples for FID, then bootstrap 1 k times to report 95 % CI; provide paired t-tests (or Wilcoxon) against each baseline at matching λ.
   • For correlation ρ in Exp-2, provide mean ± stderr across images and Bonferroni-corrected p-values.
C. Fix measurement methodology.
   • Measure FLOPs with the real gated execution path (fvcore with custom sparse-conv rules) and verify against nvprof.
   • Measure energy per-image for all models under identical sample counts and identical CUDA MPS clocks.
D. Address memory contradiction.
   • Confirm profiler runs in a separate pass with batch-size 1, or switch to torch.profiler → record_function to avoid activation storage.
E. Increase reproducibility.
   • Publish Dockerfile or conda-env + exact commit hash of every dependency.
   • Provide a colab that downloads pre-computed fake/real images and recomputes FID.
F. Add missing controls.
   • Include single-stage non-hierarchical diffusion to show DHAC’s benefit is specific to hierarchical decoders.
   • Add ablation where uncertainty head is random-initialised to prove gating learns meaningful signals.
G. Clarify energy & FLOP budgets.
   • Report absolute numbers (e.g. 16 GFLOPs→8 GFLOPs) not only speed-up factors; include error bars.
   • Quote GPU utilisation % to show sparse kernels are not merely memory-bound.

If these steps are followed the experiment would have full numerical backing, proper statistical significance and transparent measurement, raising the consistency_score into the 8–9 range.

The manuscript contains an extremely detailed experimental PLAN, but the actual RESULTS that accompany the submission are almost entirely placeholders produced by a dummy script.

Major internal-consistency problems
1. No real evaluation numbers.  All headline claims (2–3× FLOP reduction at equal FID, ≤0.4 ΔFID at 4× speed-up, etc.) are unsupported.  The quick-run logs show identical FID ≈13.23 for all datasets and “FLOPs = nan”, indicating that the sparse flop counter never executed.  Statistical tests, confidence intervals, p-values and effect sizes promised in the plan are absent.
2. Dummy models invalidate reproducibility.  The runner loads _DummyModel objects that spit out random noise; consequently every metric is meaningless with respect to diffusion models.
3. Missing baseline and control results.  No numbers for Baseline, ASE, spatial-only, temporal-only, single-stage control, or quantised models are reported, so none of the ablation or robustness claims can be checked.
4. Contradictory outcome vs. plan.  The plan says 50 k samples per condition; the actual log samples ~500 images total before finishing in seconds—far too little for a reliable FID estimate.
5. FLOP, energy and memory instrumentation never ran on GPU hardware (runs inside CI with no CUDA device).  Any comparison of efficiency is therefore invalid.

Consequences for claims
• Without real FID and FLOP numbers the core claim of “adaptive spatio-temporal gating yields 2–3× speed-up at equal image quality” is completely unsubstantiated.
• The strong statistical rhetoric (paired t-tests, Bonferroni, etc.) is irrelevant because the underlying data are missing.

Actionable steps to reach a consistency score ≥8
1. Replace dummy stubs with the actual hierarchical diffusion checkpoints and gating code; make sure the CI job runs on a GPU runner.
2. Collect full numerical tables for EXP-1–3 with 3 seeds, 50 k images per seed on ImageNet-64 and the stated 128/4 batch sizes.  Report:
   • FID ±95 % CI
   • FLOPs/img ±SD (validated against nvprof)
   • wall-clock ms/img and J/img
3. Provide the exact operating-point matching algorithm (ΔFID ≤0.2) in the analysis script so reviewers can see which rows are compared.
4. Include full ablation and control rows, even if they under-perform; this is necessary to demonstrate the causal contribution of spatial + temporal gates.
5. Release raw Parquet/CSV files as promised and add a checksum list so reviewers can verify integrity.
6. Run bootstrap or permutation tests to obtain confidence intervals for correlation (ρ) and edge-precision metrics in EXP-2.
7. Ensure FLOPs are reported in the same units (GigaFLOPs) across models and that nan values are impossible (add assert not np.isnan).
8. Add a reproducibility appendix that shows at least one independent rerun (new seed, new GPU) reproduces the 2–3× speed-up within ±5 %.
9. Tighten the energy measurement: sample NVML power every 10 ms instead of 100 ms for better temporal resolution.
10. Present one qualitative figure per experiment (e.g. gate heat-maps) side-by-side with the quantitative results to visually corroborate the numbers.

If all above steps are completed and the claimed speed-ups with rigorous statistical backing hold, the study would likely score 8–9 for consistency.

The manuscript contains a very detailed and well-thought-out experimental PLAN (EXP-1, 2, 3) but the RESULTS section does not report the outputs that the plan promises.  

Major internal inconsistencies
1. Metrics mismatch – The plan commits to reporting FID, sFID, GFLOPs/img, ms/img, Joule/img, edge-precision, gate/uncertainty correlations and a battery of statistical tests.  The only numbers that appear in the Results are classification losses/accuracies that are completely unrelated to diffusion sampling or adaptive gating.
2. Missing baselines & ablations – No numbers for Baseline-HDM-3, ASE, DHAC-λ grid, DHAC-T, DHAC-S, or Single-Stage control are shown, so none of the speed-up or quality claims can be verified.
3. No statistical evidence – the plan specifies paired t-tests, Wilcoxon tests, ANOVA, Levene tests, bootstrap CIs, etc.; none of these statistics are reported, and no p-values appear.
4. No reproducibility artefacts – the text says that Parquet/CSV files, SHA-256 checksums and Zenodo records will be provided, but none are linked or summarised.
5. Logical contradiction – The concluding paragraph claims “DHAC achieves 2–3× FLOP reduction at matched FID”.  As no FID or FLOP numbers are reported, the claim is unsupported and contradicts the evidence shown.

How to raise the consistency_score
A. Produce the promised quantitative tables.
   • For EXP-1, give a table like  “model | λ | dataset | FID (±CI) | GFLOPs/img (±SD) | speed-up | p-value”.
   • For EXP-2, report mean ρ, edge-precision, sparsity with Wilcoxon p-values and effect sizes.
   • For EXP-3, supply the 48-cell grid with FID / GFLOPs / speed-up and the outcome of the four pre-registered hypotheses.
B. Include the confidence intervals and exact p-values to demonstrate statistical significance.
C. Attach—or at least summarise—the checksums of the data files to prove that the numbers are produced by the code.
D. Supply at least one seed-level repetition to show reproducibility; the plan says three seeds plus seed-47 rerun—report them.
E. Insert plots of the Pareto curves and violin plots that the plan describes; they help the reader visually confirm claims.
F. Verify FLOP counts with nvprof and mention the agreement numbers (<2 %).
G. If space is limited, put full tables in the appendix and a condensed version in the main text, but do not omit them.

Road-map to reach a score 8-10
1. Run the full code for EXP-1-3, collect all metrics, and publish the raw Parquet files.
2. Compute the pre-registered statistical tests and include a table of p-values after Holm/Bonnferoni correction.
3. Provide effect sizes (Cohen’s d) and confidence intervals for every key comparison.
